title: Rethinking Joint Maximum Mean Discrepancy for Visual Domain Adaptation

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 3.3, Eq. (4), and all later uses of HSIC
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper defines a concise HSIC loss as tr(K^{XX}(K^{YY} ⊙ M^H)) and tr(B^{⊤}K^{XX}(K^{YY} ⊙ M^H)K^{XX}B) but never provides a definition for the matrix M^H. Without M^H, the HSIC term and the proposed joint loss JMMD-HSIC (Eq. (9)) are ambiguous and cannot be implemented or reproduced. The graph-embedding analysis that relies on M^H is therefore also unsupported.

The six per-task accuracies listed (96.1, 95.3, 77.6, 98.1, 77.1, 99.1) average to 90.55, which rounds to 90.6, not 90.1 as printed. The reported average of 90.1 is a miscalculation that distorts the results and misleads subsequent comparisons.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, sentences: 'has achieved 1.4%/0.8% and 0.9%/0.8% improvements ... OGL²P+JMMD-HSIC could achieve the best average results among all compared approaches, with 0.3% and 0.5% improvements over the second-best method, i.e., RSDA-MSTN.'
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In Table 1, OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC (90.1) is worse than OGL²P (90.7), so no 0.8% improvement exists; it is a degradation. Moreover, RSDA-MSTN (91.2) has a higher average than OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC on Office-31, so the claim that OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC is the best and improves by 0.3% over RSDA-MSTN is false. The text directly contradicts the presented data.

predicted_errors.error_location: Table 1 vs Table 3, Office-31, OGL²P+JMMD-HSIC results
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Table 1 reports OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC on Office-31 as 90.1 (average), while Table 3 (ablation study) reports 91.5 ± 1.3 for the same method on the same dataset with ResNet-50 features. The conflict (90.1 vs 91.5) is too large to be attributed to rounding or normal variance, indicating an internal data inconsistency between the two tables.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix E, proof that K^4 is a reproducing kernel
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof states: x^{⊤} G^4 x = Σ_i Σ_j w_{ij}(x_i - x_j)^2 ≥ 0. For a graph Laplacian G^4 = D − W, the correct identity is x^{⊤} G^4 x = (1/2) Σ_i Σ_j w_{ij}(x_i − x_j)^2. The missing factor 1/2 makes the claimed equality inaccurate, though the non-negativity conclusion remains valid.
